operatorOutcome: `node --test scripts/runtime/landos-runtime.test.mjs` passes in any checkout of this repository, including a git worktree or CI checkout whose directory is not named `claudeclaw-os`, while still proving that sanitizeEnvironment sets LANDOS_RUNTIME_ROOT to the repository root.
builderBrief:
Fix a real defect in this repository's runtime test suite.

`scripts/runtime/landos-runtime.test.mjs` contains the test `environment sanitizer deduplicates PATH casing and keeps useful entries`. Its last assertion is:

    assert.equal(result.LANDOS_RUNTIME_ROOT.toLowerCase().endsWith('claudeclaw-os'), true);

That asserts the checkout directory is named `claudeclaw-os`. It passes only by accident of one machine's folder name. In a git worktree, a clone under another name, or a CI checkout, this single assertion fails while the other twelve tests pass, so the suite reports a false failure. Confirm it yourself: this working directory is not named `claudeclaw-os`, and `node --test scripts/runtime/landos-runtime.test.mjs` currently fails on exactly that line.

The production code is correct. `sanitizeEnvironment` sets `LANDOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` to `ROOT`, the repository root the module computes from its own location, and `ROOT` is already imported by this test file. The test's expectation is the thing that is wrong.

Repair the assertion so it proves the real property: that `LANDOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is the repository root of whatever checkout the suite is running in, independent of that directory's name. Keep the assertion meaningful; do not delete it, do not weaken it to something trivially true, and do not remove any other test. Change nothing outside `scripts/runtime/landos-runtime.test.mjs`; the runtime module itself must not be touched.

No third-party dependencies are available in this working directory, and none are needed.
